title: When the Sigil Burns
premise: Emrys Ishikawa, a temple scribe indentured to pay their late mother's debts, survives by mapping smuggler routes and keeping their head down—until a dying pilgrim presses a burning sigil into their palm and the forgotten god Thorn answers their half-prayer aloud. Hunted by the usurper Vaelric's inquisitors and bound to a covenant the gods themselves broke, Emrys must cross the Thornfell mountains with a disgraced knight and a heretic priestess to reforge the pact that once held the realms together. At the Gates of Ash, Emrys learns the covenant demands a memory as payment, and the only one that can seal it is their own: every recollection of who they loved and who they were. In the end Emrys chooses to burn the sigil and themselves into the new covenant—remembering nothing, becoming the living law that turns Vaelric's armies back—and wakes in the free cities as a stranger the whole world somehow trusts.
about_author: M. M. Vane is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction full-time. Their work blends pilgrimage narratives with quiet, aching love stories, and they write in a cabin at the edge of a forest they refuse to name.

chapters.title: Ink Owed to the Temple
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. We meet Emrys copying ledgers in the Temple of Quiet Hours, counting the years left on their mother's debt, and secretly selling smuggler routes to keep the interest at bay. The emotional beat is weary self-containment: Emrys has made smallness an art, and believes invisibility is safety.

chapters.title: The Pilgrim Who Knew My Name
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A pilgrim collapses at the temple gate, burned from the inside, and presses a hot iron sigil into Emrys's palm with their name already known. That night, the mountain itself answers a half-whispered prayer. The beat is dread laced with a terrible thrill of being seen.

chapters.title: What the Abbot Cannot Unsee
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, with a brief shift to Abbot Corvane. The sigil won't cool, and the abbot—terrified of Vaelric's inquisitors—gives Emrys one night to flee, forgiving a fraction of the debt as severance or sentence. The beat is betrayal softened by pity: even kindness here is exile.

chapters.title: A Knight with a Broken Oath
chapters.summary: Ser Aldric's POV. Emrys is caught by Aldric Vane, a knight who deserted Vaelric's army after being ordered to burn a village of god-touched children. He needs a guide through Thornfell; Emrys needs protection. The beat is wary, transactional alliance with an undertow of mutual recognition.

chapters.title: Roads Only Smugglers Remember
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The two traverse a pass that appears on no map, and the sigil warms whenever Emrys chooses the old paths—suggesting the god is steering them. Emrys resents being a puppet. The beat is resistance: identity as something you defend route by route.

chapters.title: The Heretic of Hollowbridge
chapters.summary: Priestess Sefa's POV. In a river town, the trio recruits Sefa, a priestess excommunicated for insisting the old gods never died, only went silent. She reads the sigil and names it the Covenant Mark. The beat is hope arriving in an unwelcome shape: the truth Emrys wanted to deny.

chapters.title: Inquisitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Maren's POV. We see the hunt through enemy eyes: Maren tracks the sigil's heat with a stolen relic and a cold certainty that Emrys is not a threat but a key. The beat is chilling competence—Vaelric's machine is patient, and patience is more frightening than cruelty.

chapters.title: Prayers in the Burnt Orchard
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Sheltering in an orchard destroyed by Vaelric's purge, Emrys prays again—deliberately this time—and Thorn speaks: the covenant broke because the gods took memories as payment and the last bearer refused. The beat is grief; Emrys begins to understand the price ahead.

chapters.title: What Aldric Left in the Ashes
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. Ambushed by his former company, Aldric confesses the village he failed to save—and that he recognized the sigil because he carried one once, and gave it up. The beat is shame met with unexpected grace; Emrys and Aldric stop being employer and guide.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Breathe Uneasy
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The trio reaches Meridian, a free city preparing for siege, where the council wants to use Emrys as a bargaining chip with Vaelric. Sefa argues for the covenant instead. The beat is political claustrophobia: love and duty now wear the faces of institutions.

chapters.title: A Night That Owes Nothing
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Before the council's verdict, Emrys and Aldric spend one stolen night on the city walls, admitting what they've become to each other. The beat is tenderness sharpened by foreknowledge: Emrys already suspects the covenant will demand exactly this memory.

chapters.title: The Council of Small Candles
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The council votes to trade Emrys; Sefa and Aldric break them out, and Emrys chooses the mountains over safety for the first time in their life. The beat is agency seized: invisibility ends not with a battle but with a decision to be someone.

chapters.title: Maren's Mercy
chapters.summary: Inquisitor Maren's POV. Maren captures Sefa and offers Emrys a bargain: the sigil for Sefa's life, revealing that Maren once prayed to Thorn too and was answered with silence. The beat is tragic symmetry—hunter and hunted are the same wound, differently dressed.

chapters.title: The Gates of Ash
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. The trio reaches the covenant's birthplace, a gate of fused glass and bone where the last bearer's refusal is still written in the rock. Thorn shows Emrys the full price: one memory, freely given, and it will not let Emrys choose which. The beat is holy terror.

chapters.title: Vaelric Descends
chapters.summary: Vaelric's POV, his first. The usurper arrives with his army, and we learn he broke the covenant deliberately: a god who owes you nothing cannot demand your memories. The beat is ideological clarity—Vaelric is Emrys's future if they choose safety over selfhood.

chapters.title: Sefa's Last Rite
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Rescued but dying from Maren's interrogation, Sefa completes the rite's first half and gives Emrys her own memory of the old gods as a bridge. The beat is sacrifice as inheritance: faith passed hand to hand like a candle in wind.

chapters.title: The Choice of One Memory
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. At the gate, Thorn offers Emrys a loophole: give a false memory, a small one, and the covenant will hold—imperfectly, temporarily. The beat is temptation rendered gentle, which makes it monstrous. Emrys sees Vaelric's whole life in that offer.

chapters.title: When the Sigil Burns
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, climax. As Vaelric's vanguard hits the gate, Emrys gives the covenant everything—the wall-top night, their mother's voice, their own name—reforging the pact as the sigil immolates them. The beat is ecstatic loss: love against duty resolved by becoming the duty itself.

chapters.title: The Armies That Turned Back
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The new covenant manifests as a living law in the mountains; Vaelric's soldiers find their oaths dissolving and retreat. Aldric holds Emrys's body and rages at a god that saves the world by taking the one person he—. The beat is grief with the sentence unfinished.

chapters.title: Maren Kneels
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. The inquisitor, her relic gone silent and her god audible again, kneels at the gate and hears Thorn answer her childhood prayer at last. The beat is devastating grace: the antagonist's arc closes not in defeat but in being heard.

chapters.title: A Stranger in the Free Cities
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Emrys wakes in Meridian with no past, known by everyone and knowing no one, the covenant's law written in their pulse. Aldric approaches as a stranger with a familiar gentleness. The beat is fragile beginning: identity as something that can be rebuilt, not only lost.

chapters.title: The First New Prayer
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, coda. Emrys, now the temple's living covenant, writes their first ledger line—not a debt but a gift—and lets Aldric teach them their own story one evening at a time. The beat is quiet hope: memory ends, but love, given freely, can be learned again.
